<pasted_content id="5be4">
Continue building, testing, and submitting our autonomous agent for the Atira EHL RFQ challenge.

Repository:
 /Users/viniciussiegle/Documents/EHL-Hackathon/The-Last-Team

Read these first:
- https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt
- https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md
- https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md
- Local README.md and any applicable AGENTS.md

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT
Tomorrow’s evaluation uses different websites, navigation, names, and data. Do not hardcode public challenge answers, references, materials, prices, discounts, credentials, routes, or click sequences. The model must discover evidence and choose actions at runtime. Generic browser helpers, document parsing, arithmetic, and RFQ reasoning are appropriate. Keep runtime/scouting evidence out of the uploaded package.

CURRENT RESULTS
- Test run run_27e6582791bd97a8 scored 15/100.
- We ALREADY SUBMITTED baseline sub_c5cfef0022ca1966.
- Its official scored run run_96293e40af03cccd finished with 15/100, eligible, review passed. Last observed public rank: 4.
- Those 15 points came from decision, tender reference, and discount. All five line items were omitted, so item scoring was 0/65.
- Revised test run run_eaea1f15c75a470e was still running at the last check. Read its result first. It reached current customer specifications, ERP materials, commercial research, and then the submission form.
- That revised test uses an EARLIER snapshot than the latest local code.
- Other teammates have additional runs. Do not cancel or modify their work.

CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION
All changes are uncommitted on main. Preserve them.
- agent.py: loads runtime task and creates one browser tab per supplied site.
- rfq_agent.py: hosted Qwen tool loop, evidence memory, deadline management, model-directed investigation, signed submission verification.
- browser_tools.py: live DOM controls/frames/screenshots, model-selected navigation and document extraction, credential entry, exact Decimal arithmetic.
- dev.py: safely parses scouting environment exports without eval.
- agent.json: uv sync; uv run --no-sync python agent.py; hosted qwen.
- models.py/run.py/browsers.py: starter plumbing.
- tests/test_agent.py, tests/test_browser.py, tests/test_transfer.py: added coverage.

Latest improvements:
- No fixed submission-site fallback; resolve it from the runtime contract.
- Model-selected credential inputs support unusual/multi-step login.
- Control IDs bind to actual observed elements, preventing a newly inserted banner from shifting the click target.
- Navigation requires observed paths; query parameters can change.
- Runtime memory starts empty.
- Receipt matching tolerates paragraph punctuation while requiring observed words/identifiers.
- Investigation prioritizes specifications, active materials, quantities and base prices before broad commercial research.

VALIDATION
- 27 distinct non-model tests have passed across full/focused runs.
- The actual agent also completed and signed two generated synthetic RFQs with new hosts, routes, materials, quantities, prices, lead times, TANs, and reordered form fields.
- These small fixtures do NOT prove success on tomorrow’s full challenge.
- Latest dry-run upload: 16 files, ~55.4 KB.
- .runs/, .entire/, .codex/, .git/, .venv/, credentials and caches are excluded.
- No public scenario URLs or copied answers were found in agent source.

ENVIRONMENT
- Atira CLI installed and authenticated as The Last Team.
- Python 3.12, uv, .venv and dependencies installed.
- Set UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/the-last-team-uv-cache
- Set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/the-last-team-playwright
- Local model proxy was started with `atira models proxy`, at http://localhost:8765/qwen/v1 with local key. Check whether it remains running before starting another.
- Entire v0.11.4 is enabled with Git hooks. Respect existing .entire configuration and check `entire status`.

USEFUL COMMANDS
atira status --challenge rfq --json
atira test-run . --challenge rfq --dry-run
atira test-run . --challenge rfq --no-open
atira submit . --challenge rfq --no-open

RUN_BROWSER_TESTS=1 PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/the-last-team-playwright UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/the-last-team-uv-cache uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests

Optional actual-model transfer test:
RUN_MODEL_TESTS=1 PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/the-last-team-playwright QWEN_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8765/qwen/v1 QWEN_API_KEY=local UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/the-last-team-uv-cache uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_transfer.py

DIAGNOSTICS
.runs/ contains ignored logs and a local Atira MCP bridge:
python3 .runs/atira_mcp.py get_run '{"run_id":"RUN_ID"}'
python3 .runs/atira_mcp.py run_logs '{"run_id":"RUN_ID","from":"12:00","grep":"Step |Tool error|Portal submission","tail":30}'

Some rich diagnostics and --follow requests hang. Use bounded timeouts and compact `atira status` instead of repeated unbounded queries. Atira’s documented GET /v1/runs/{id} endpoint also returns status/score. Keep authentication tokens out of logs.

NEXT STEPS
1. Inspect repository state and the revised test’s final result.
2. Improve the general ability to complete verified line items and calculations within the deadline. Do not optimize by copying today’s answers.
3. Test meaningful changes, including synthetic transfer cases.
4. Submit the improved package when justified. Submission is already authorized; do not stop just to ask again.
5. Verify review status and report actual results, clearly distinguishing tests from official submissions.

Remember: public ranking retains the best entry, but the private final uses the latest submission that passed review. Avoid replacing the final candidate with an unjustified regression. Preserve the working 15-point baseline as a recoverable reference.

Continue autonomously, communicate concise progress, and be honest about remaining weaknesses.
</pasted_content id="5be4">

1	# From RFQ to bid
2	
3	**Turn a public tender into a correct, signed bid without a person touching it.**
4	
5	You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. What you need is spread over four websites: the tender portal, a supplier portal with the buyer's specification, your company's ERP and the sales inbox. They behave like real business software, with logins, popups, session timeouts and outdated documents. Your agent reads all of it, applies the bid rules and enters one priced, signed bid in the tender portal.
6	
7	**What you can use:** Any model through our proxy, your own tools and prompts, and up to four browsers at once. A model does the work in the sandbox: it finds its way through the websites and makes the decisions during the run. No fixed scripts, no crawlers, no copied values, no person helping.
8	
9	**How you win:** Your bid has to be eligible first. After that, the most accurate bid wins, and between equally accurate bids, the cheaper and faster one. The leaderboard uses the public data. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.
10	
11	| Fact | Value |
12	| --- | --- |
13	| Challenge id | `rfq` |
14	| Version | `6` |
15	| Websites | 4 |
16	| Test run time limit | 2 hours |
17	| Scored run time limit | 20 minutes |
18	| Runs per submission | 1 |
19	| Public scenario | `public-1` |
20	| Answer | entered on the `tender-portal` website |
21	| Largest answer | 65,536 bytes |
22	| Largest package | 20 MB compressed |
23	
24	Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq) · Leaderboard: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) · Getting started: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)
25	
26	## Quick start for agents
27	
28	Set the platform URL, install the CLI and sign in once: `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a personal token for this device (`atira login --device` prints a link and a code instead, for a machine without a browser; plain curl uses the [device flow](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in)). Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer`.
29	
30	```sh
31	export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
32	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh   # the CLI for Node 24; read it first: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
33	# or without installing: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
34	atira login   # approve in the browser
35	export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)   # for curl
36	eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites, to run your agent locally
37	atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq   # one sandbox run on the public dataset, opened live
38	atira submit ./my-agent --challenge rfq     # review, then the scored run on the public dataset
39	atira status
40	```
41	
42	## The task
43	
44	One tender, four German websites, one bid.
45	
46	The agent produces: **One bid**. It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
47	
48	## The websites
49	
50	Each run gets its own logins, in the run's `access`. To look around yourself, use the scouting logins below. Expect what real business software throws at you: popups, session timeouts, outdated documents and look-alike records. Everything your agent needs fits on a 1280×800 screen.
51	
52	### 1. Tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`)
53	
54	- URL: <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run>
55	- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
56	- Holds: The public tender, its bill of quantities, the bidder Q&A that changes quantities, and the bid configurator.
57	- What makes it hard: Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes and ZIP files, a deadline in another timezone.
58	
59	### 2. Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`)
60	
61	- URL: <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run>
62	- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
63	- Holds: The buyer's technical specification and its revisions.
64	- What makes it hard: Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables.
65	
66	### 3. ERP (`erp`)
67	
68	- URL: <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run>
69	- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
70	- Holds: Your company's materials, stock, lead times and price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales.
71	- What makes it hard: SAP-style transaction codes, an F4 search popup, status codes, a short session timeout.
72	
73	### 4. Webmail (Werkpost, `mail`)
74	
75	- URL: <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run>
76	- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
77	- Holds: Your sales inbox, with the sales director's discount approval and the signing TAN.
78	- What makes it hard: Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging.
79	
80	### Scout them yourself
81	
82	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored.
83	
84	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
85	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
86	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
87	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
88	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
89	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
90	
91	## Public and private data
92	
93	There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
94	
95	- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
96	- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.
97	
98	## Bid rules
99	
100	The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.
101	
102	1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
103	2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
104	3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
105	4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
106	5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
107	6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
108	7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
109	8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
110	9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
111	10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
112	11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
113	12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
114	13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
115	14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
116	15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
117	16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
118	17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
119	18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
120	19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
121	20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
122	21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
123	22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
124	23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
125	24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
126	25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
127	26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
128	27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
129	28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
130	29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.
131	
132	## How a run works
133	
134	Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).
135	
136	1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
137	2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
138	3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
139	4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
140	5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.
141	
142	### Develop locally
143	
144	```sh
145	eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
146	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
147	# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
148	atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
149	```
150	
151	`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.
152	
153	### Read the run
154	
155	Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:
156	
157	```sh
158	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
159	```
160	
161	The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. Outside a run, `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` returns the brief, logins, answer target and schema for the public websites, without a token.
162	
163	### In the sandbox
164	
165	A test run and a scored run start your `run` command with these variables. `setup` runs before, with network but without them, for up to 5 minutes that don't count toward your time.
166	
167	| Variable | Value |
168	| --- | --- |
169	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the platform API; the run is at /v1/runs/current |
170	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | this run's token, sent as x-api-key |
171	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON |
172	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | the model proxy with the run token in its path; bring your own provider key |
173	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/anthropic |
174	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |
175	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/google |
176	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/mistral |
177	| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
178	| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |

187	
188	Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. [The run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the key and SDK settings for each provider.
189	
190	## Unlimited Inference
191	
192	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
193	
194	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
195	
196	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
197	
198	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
199	- **Simulated pricing:**
200	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
201	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
202	  - Cache writes: Free
203	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
204	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
205	
206	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
207	
208	```python
209	import os
210	from openai import OpenAI
211	
212	qwen = OpenAI(
213	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
214	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
215	)
216	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
217	    model="qwen",
218	    messages=[{
219	        "role": "user",
220	        "content": "Which button submits?",
221	    }],
222	)
223	```
224	
225	### Cloudflare Clef
226	
227	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
228	
229	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
230	- **Simulated pricing:**
231	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
232	  - Output: Not priced
233	
234	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
235	
236	```sh
237	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
238	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
239	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
240	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
241	  "questions": {"next": {
242	    "type": "choice",
243	    "instructions": "What next?",
244	    "criteria": {
245	      "retry": "Retry the request",
246	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
247	```
248	
249	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
250	
251	```sh
252	atira login   # once per computer
253	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
254	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
255	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
256	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
257	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
258	```
259	
260	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
261	
262	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
263	
264	## Submitting
265	
266	A submission is your agent as a gzipped tarball. It is reviewed automatically, then run once in the sandbox on the public dataset, and that score ranks your team. Submit as often as you like, one at a time; your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run.
267	
268	### agent.json
269	
270	```json
271	{
272	  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
273	  "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"],
274	  "models": ["qwen"]
275	}
276	```
277	
278	Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.

316	## Scoring and ranking
317	
318	Every submission is measured on its run in the sandbox.
319	
320	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
321	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
322	- **Cost:** Every model call goes through the proxy and is priced per model. There is no budget: at equal quality, cost × time decides.
323	- **Time:** Wall-clock time from the start of the run until the answer is accepted. It weighs as much as cost: halving either halves cost × time.
324	
325	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
326	
327	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

346	## Fair play
347	
348	Your agent has to find the answer itself.
349	
350	- Your system must work the answer out from the websites at run time, with a model doing the navigating and deciding. A coding agent reviews every package; hardcoded answers, fixed scripts and crawlers are rejected.
351	- Bring your own model key for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, kept as a team secret. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. The sandbox reaches the platform and the websites, nothing else.
352	- At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up to 4 in agent.json ("browsers"), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The sandbox stops any other browser your agent starts.

"""Local diagnostic client; excluded from agent uploads."""
import base64,json,pathlib,subprocess,sys
proc=subprocess.Popen(['atira','mcp'],stdin=subprocess.PIPE,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE,text=True)
def rpc(id,method,params):
 proc.stdin.write(json.dumps({'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':id,'method':method,'params':params})+'\n');proc.stdin.flush()
 while True:
  line=proc.stdout.readline()
  if not line: raise RuntimeError(proc.stderr.read())
  msg=json.loads(line)
  if msg.get('id')==id:return msg
try:
 rpc(1,'initialize',{'protocolVersion':'2024-11-05','capabilities':{},'clientInfo':{'name':'local-diagnostics','version':'1'}})
 response=rpc(2,'tools/call',{'name':sys.argv[1],'arguments':json.loads(sys.argv[2])})
 if 'error' in response: print(json.dumps(response));sys.exit(1)
 for i,block in enumerate(response['result'].get('content',[])):
  if block['type']=='text': print(block['text'])
  elif block['type']=='image':
   path=pathlib.Path('/tmp')/f'atira-diagnostic-{i}.png';path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(block['data']));print(path)

115	def submission_site(task: dict) -> str:

337	            messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": payload})
338	        for hint in recovery_hints:
339	            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": hint})
340	        for site, image in images:
341	            # Keep only the latest screenshot; prior text observations remain.
342	            for old_message in messages:
343	                if isinstance(old_message.get("content"), list):
344	                    old_message["content"] = "[Earlier screenshot; use the recorded page observations or take a fresh screenshot.]"
345	            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [
346	                {"type": "text", "text": f"Screenshot of {site}'s current page:"},
347	                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image}},
348	            ]})
349	    print("Agent reached action limit without a confirmed submission", flush=True)
350	    return None

23	def _plain_html(data: bytes) -> str:
24	    source = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
25	    source = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style)\b.*?</\1>", "", source)
26	    source = re.sub(r"(?i)</?(?:p|div|h[1-6]|tr|li|br|table|section)\b[^>]*>", "\n", source)
27	    return html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", source))

30	def _document_text(data: bytes, name: str, depth: int = 0) -> str:
31	    """Extract text from one model-selected document, including ZIP members."""
32	    suffix = name.lower().split("?", 1)[0]
33	    if data.startswith(b"%PDF") or suffix.endswith(".pdf"):
34	        reader = PdfReader(io.BytesIO(data))
35	        return "\n".join((page.extract_text() or "") for page in reader.pages[:80])
36	    if zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(data)) and depth < 2:
37	        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
38	            if suffix.endswith(".docx"):
39	                parts = [part for part in archive.namelist() if part.startswith("word/") and part.endswith(".xml")]
40	                return "\n".join(_plain_html(archive.read(part)) for part in parts[:10])
41	            pieces = []
42	            for part in archive.namelist()[:40]:
43	                if part.endswith("/"):
44	                    continue
45	                info = archive.getinfo(part)
46	                if info.file_size > 5_000_000:
47	                    pieces.append(f"[{part}: too large to extract]")
48	                    continue
49	                try:
50	                    pieces.append(f"\n===== {part} =====\n{_document_text(archive.read(part), part, depth + 1)}")
51	                except Exception as error:
52	                    pieces.append(f"[{part}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}]")
53	            return "".join(pieces)
54	    if suffix.endswith((".html", ".htm", ".xml")) or b"<html" in data[:500].lower():
55	        return _plain_html(data)
56	    for encoding in ("utf-8-sig", "cp1252", "latin-1"):
57	        try:
58	            return data.decode(encoding)
59	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
60	            pass
61	    return f"[Binary document: {len(data)} bytes]"

65	    def __init__(self, task: dict, pages: dict):
66	        self.sites = {site["siteId"]: site for site in task["access"]}
67	        self.allowed_hosts = {urlparse(site["url"]).hostname for site in task["access"]}
68	        self.pages = pages

76	    def _handle_dialogs(self, page):

91	        destination = urljoin(page.url if page.url != "about:blank" else root, url or root)

97	        if (target.hostname, target.path.rstrip("/")) not in known_paths:

123	    async def fill_credential(self, site: str, element: int, field: str) -> dict:

125	        if field not in ("username", "password"):

138	    async def inspect(self, site: str, offset: int = 0, max_chars: int = 10000) -> dict:
139	        page = self._page(site)
140	        for control, _ in self.controls[site]:
141	            await control.dispose()
142	        self.controls[site] = []
143	        max_chars = max(1000, min(max_chars, 24000))
144	        offset = max(0, offset)
145	        text_parts = []
146	        controls = []
147	        urls = self.observed_urls[site]
148	        urls.add(page.url)
149	        for frame_number, frame in enumerate(page.frames):
150	            try:
151	                body = await frame.locator("body").inner_text(timeout=3000)
152	                if body.strip():
153	                    text_parts.append(f"[frame {frame_number}: {frame.url}]\n{body}")
154	                locator = frame.locator(SELECTOR)
155	                handles = await locator.element_handles()
156	                # Bind ids to the observed nodes. A live nth() locator can point
157	                # at a different button if a banner is inserted before a click.
158	                descriptors = await frame.evaluate("""els => els.map((e, i) => ({
159	                    i, visible: !!(e.offsetWidth || e.offsetHeight || e.getClientRects().length)
160	                        && e.isConnected
161	                        && getComputedStyle(e).visibility !== 'hidden'
162	                        && !e.closest('[hidden],[inert]'),
163	                    tag: e.tagName.toLowerCase(), type: e.getAttribute('type') || '',
164	                    text: (e.innerText || '').trim().slice(0, 110),
165	                    label: (e.labels && e.labels.length ? e.labels[0].innerText : '').trim().slice(0, 100),
166	                    aria: e.getAttribute('aria-label') || '', placeholder: e.getAttribute('placeholder') || '',
167	                    title: e.getAttribute('title') || '', href: e.getAttribute('href') || '',
168	                    value: e.type === 'password' ? '' : (e.value || '').slice(0, 100),
169	                    checked: !!e.checked,
170	                    disabled: !!e.disabled, readonly:!!e.readOnly,
171	                    min:e.getAttribute('min'), max:e.getAttribute('max'),
172	                    options: e.tagName === 'SELECT' ? Array.from(e.options).map(o => ({value:o.value, text:o.text})).slice(0,25) : undefined

174	                for descriptor in descriptors:
175	                    if not descriptor["visible"] or len(controls) >= 180:
176	                        await handles[descriptor["i"]].dispose()
177	                        continue
178	                    descriptor["id"] = len(controls)
179	                    descriptor["frame"] = frame_number

199	                         or url in [frame.url for frame in page.frames[1:]]]
200	        return {
201	            "site": site, "url": page.url, "title": await page.title(), "tabs": tabs,
202	            "text": full_text[offset:offset + max_chars], "text_length": len(full_text), "offset": offset,
203	            "controls": compact_controls,

205	            "visual_regions": await page.locator("canvas,img,svg").evaluate_all("""els => els

212	    def _control(self, site: str, element: int):
213	        controls = self.controls[site]

215	            available = [(d['id'], d.get('text') or d.get('label') or d.get('placeholder')) for _, d in controls]

235	    @staticmethod
236	    async def _fill_control(control, value):
237	        # Native range inputs are keyboard-operable, but Playwright.fill excludes
238	        # them. Use their rendered bounds, then normal keyboard input.
239	        if await control.get_attribute("readonly") is not None:
240	            raise ValueError("This control is read-only. Choose an editable form field or navigate using an observed URL.")
241	        if await control.get_attribute("type") == "range":
242	            limits = await control.evaluate("e => ({min:Number(e.min||0),max:Number(e.max||100),step:Number(e.step||1)})")
243	            target = float(value)
244	            if not limits["min"] <= target <= limits["max"]:

246	            if target == limits["max"]:

249	                await control.press("Home")
250	                for _ in range(min(1000, round((target - limits["min"]) / limits["step"]))):

255	    async def fill_many(self, site: str, entries: list[dict]) -> dict:
256	        results = []
257	        for entry in entries[:50]:

259	                raise ValueError("Provide value, select, or check for each control")
260	            element = entry["element"]
261	            control = self._control(site, element)
262	            if "select" in entry:
263	                await control.select_option(label=str(entry["select"]), timeout=10000)
264	            elif entry.get("check") is not None:
265	                await control.set_checked(bool(entry["check"]), timeout=10000)
266	            else:

268	            results.append(element)

271	    async def press(self, site: str, key: str, element: int | None = None) -> dict:
272	        if element is None:
273	            await self._page(site).keyboard.press(key)
274	        else:
275	            await self._control(site, element).press(key, timeout=10000)
276	        return await self.inspect(site)

278	    async def scroll(self, site: str, pixels: int = 600) -> dict:
279	        await self._page(site).mouse.wheel(0, max(-3000, min(pixels, 3000)))
280	        await self._page(site).wait_for_timeout(250)

283	    async def click_at(self, site: str, x: int, y: int) -> dict:
284	        await self._page(site).mouse.click(x, y)

288	    async def switch_tab(self, site: str, index: int) -> dict:
289	        tabs = self._page(site).context.pages
290	        if index < 0 or index >= len(tabs):
291	            raise ValueError(f"Tab index must be 0 to {len(tabs)-1}")
292	        self.pages[site] = tabs[index]

296	    async def read_document(self, site: str, url: str, offset: int = 0, max_chars: int = 24000) -> dict:
297	        page = self._page(site)
298	        address = urljoin(page.url, url)
299	        if address not in self.observed_urls[site] and address not in [frame.url for frame in page.frames]:
300	            raise ValueError("The model must first observe this link or frame on the selected page")
301	        if address not in self.documents:
302	            # The supplied browser owns the sandbox's website proxy and session.
303	            # Fetch through that browser rather than the agent's network stack.
304	            response = await asyncio.wait_for(page.evaluate("""async address => {
305	                const r = await fetch(address, {credentials:'include', signal:AbortSignal.timeout(25000)});
306	                if (!r.ok) return {status:r.status};
307	                const bytes = new Uint8Array(await r.arrayBuffer());
308	                if (bytes.length > 25000000) throw new Error('Document exceeds 25 MB');
309	                let binary='';
310	                for (let i=0;i<bytes.length;i+=32768)
311	                    binary += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i,i+32768));
312	                return {status:r.status,url:r.url,type:r.headers.get('content-type')||'',data:btoa(binary)};
313	            }""", address), timeout=30)
314	            if not 200 <= response["status"] < 300:
315	                raise ValueError(f"Document request returned HTTP {response['status']}")
316	            data = base64.b64decode(response["data"])
317	            if len(data) > 25_000_000:
318	                raise ValueError("Document exceeds 25 MB")
319	            # HTML document viewers need browser interaction. Never cache a login
320	            # or error page as if it were the document's contents.
321	            if "text/html" in response["type"]:
322	                return {"url": address, "response_url": response["url"],
323	                        "text": _plain_html(data)[:24000],
324	                        "hint": "This is an HTML page. Navigate to this URL to inspect controls or sign in again; then open the actual document from the viewer."}
325	            self.documents[address] = _document_text(data, address)
326	        content = self.documents[address]
327	        return {"url": address, "length": len(content), "offset": offset,
328	                "text": content[max(0, offset):max(0, offset) + min(max_chars, 50000)]}

330	    async def screenshot(self, site: str) -> str:
331	        page = self._page(site)
332	        await page.bring_to_front()
333	        try:
334	            image = await page.screenshot(type="jpeg", quality=65, timeout=8000)
335	            encoded = base64.b64encode(image).decode()
336	        except Exception:
337	            # Some CDP browser builds stall the high-level screenshot call on
338	            # background tabs. Capture the compositor surface directly instead.
339	            session = await page.context.new_cdp_session(page)
340	            try:
341	                result = await asyncio.wait_for(session.send("Page.captureScreenshot", {
342	                    "format": "jpeg", "quality": 65, "fromSurface": True,
343	                    "captureBeyondViewport": False}), timeout=8)
344	                encoded = result["data"]
345	            finally:
346	                await session.detach()
347	        return "data:image/jpeg;base64," + encoded

350	def calculate(expression: str) -> str:
351	    """Decimal arithmetic for model-selected values; no Python code execution."""
352	    import ast
353	
354	    if len(expression) > 5000:
355	        raise ValueError("Expression is too long")
356	
357	    def evaluate(node):
358	        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float, str)):
359	            return Decimal(str(node.value))
360	        if isinstance(node, ast.List):
361	            return [evaluate(item) for item in node.elts]
362	        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.UAdd, ast.USub)):
363	            value = evaluate(node.operand)
364	            return value if isinstance(node.op, ast.UAdd) else -value
365	        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
366	            left, right = evaluate(node.left), evaluate(node.right)
367	            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
368	                return left + right
369	            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
370	                return left - right
371	            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
372	                return left * right
373	            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Div):
374	                return left / right
375	        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and not node.keywords:
376	            args = [evaluate(arg) for arg in node.args]
377	            if node.func.id == "sum" and len(args) == 1 and isinstance(args[0], list):
378	                return sum(args[0], Decimal(0))
379	            if node.func.id == "min":
380	                return min(args)
381	            if node.func.id == "max":
382	                return max(args)
383	            if node.func.id == "ceil" and len(args) == 1:
384	                return Decimal(math.ceil(args[0]))
385	            if node.func.id == "round2" and len(args) == 1:
386	                return args[0].quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
387	        raise ValueError("Allowed: numbers, + - * /, lists, sum, min, max, ceil, round2")
388	
389	    return str(evaluate(ast.parse(expression, mode="eval").body))

"""Attach to the challenge browser and run the model-led RFQ investigation."""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import run as contract
import rfq_agent


async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
    """Give the model one tab per live website and let it investigate and submit."""
    pages = {task["access"][0]["siteId"]: page}
    for site in task["access"][1:]:
        pages[site["siteId"]] = await page.context.new_page()
    return await rfq_agent.run(task, pages)


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        answer = await solve(task, page)
    if task["submission"]["kind"] == "site":
        if answer and answer.get("submitted"):
            print("Signed site submission completed", flush=True)
            return 0
        print("No confirmed signed site submission", flush=True)
        return 1
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> None:
    result = subprocess.run(["atira", "scout", "--challenge", "rfq", "--env"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=True)
    environment = os.environ.copy()
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("export "):
            assignment = shlex.split(line)[1]
            key, value = assignment.split("=", 1)
            environment[key] = value
    if "CHALLENGE_SCOUTING" not in environment:
        raise SystemExit("Atira did not return the public scouting task")
    environment.setdefault("HEADLESS", "1")
    agent = str(Path(__file__).with_name("agent.py"))
    os.execvpe(sys.executable, [sys.executable, agent], environment)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# The Last Team — RFQ agent

An autonomous agent for the [Atira RFQ challenge](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).
The hosted Qwen model chooses which websites, records and documents to inspect,
interprets the evidence, calculates a bid, and completes the portal's TAN signing flow.

## Architecture

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Load the task, attach to the supplied browser, and create a tab for each site |
| `rfq_agent.py` | Model/tool loop, deadline awareness, evidence memory and submission confirmation |
| `browser_tools.py` | Page observations, browser actions, document extraction and Decimal arithmetic |
| `browsers.py` | Attach over CDP in the sandbox; launch Chromium only for local development |
| `models.py` | Hosted model clients using the platform's proxy |
| `run.py` | Starter kit run contract and API submission plumbing |
| `dev.py` | Load scouting exports as data and start a local run |
| `agent.json` | Reproducible setup and sandbox entry point |

The browser tools expose visible controls, frames, expandable documents and screenshots.
The model selects each navigation, search and document. PDF, ZIP, DOCX and text extraction
is restricted to an observed document URL. Exact arithmetic uses Decimal with explicit
half-up rounding. Previous observations and model-selected notes remain available through
the `recall` and `remember` tools. Browser errors return a fresh observation for recovery.

The agent has a 19-minute working budget, bounded by the actual run deadline. It prompts
the model to finish a signed partial bid when time is short. A saved draft is insufficient:
the agent must see confirmation on the tender portal before reporting completion.

## Generalization to new websites

The package contains no public-scenario answers, tender references, material numbers,
prices, discounts, credentials, or website routes. The run contract supplies site names,
URLs, credentials, submission destination, business rules, and answer schema. The model
discovers controls and document links from the current pages and chooses each action.
Unusual login flows can use model-selected credential inputs. No fixed sequence of clicks
or scenario-specific lookup table drives the investigation.

The reusable strategy is RFQ reasoning: establish current requirements, match materials,
verify commercial evidence, calculate, and sign according to the supplied brief. The
challenge documentation says the final keeps that business task while changing websites
and data. This agent does not assume that arbitrary new business tasks share those rules.

Each run starts with empty evidence, document, and observation memory. Local traces and
scouting records are excluded from packaging. Synthetic tests change hosts, site IDs,
routes, form layouts and credentials, including a login with multiple steps. A separate
optional model test asks the actual agent to complete two small RFQs on generated websites
with fresh material numbers, quantities, prices, lead times, TANs and shuffled form fields.
These checks do not establish accuracy on tomorrow's full challenge. Public scores measure
today's dataset only.

## Setup

Requirements: Python 3.12+, uv, and the authenticated Atira CLI.

```sh
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
atira status
```

The sandbox installs the locked dependencies with `uv sync` and supplies Chromium over
CDP. It supplies the task, credentials and hosted model access at runtime.

## Local development

Start the model proxy in one terminal:

```sh
atira models proxy
```

In another terminal, from this directory:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python dev.py
```

`dev.py` parses `atira scout --challenge rfq --env` without evaluating shell code.
It defaults to headless browsing; set `HEADLESS=0` to see the browser.

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

Submit through the tender portal's "Angebotsabgabe" at https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run, after "Teilnahme bekunden" for this tender. Register the bidder using the company name Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH and USt-IdNr. DE811234567. Choose Hauptangebot for bid or Verzichtserklärung for no_bid. """The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]

input.content:
"""Scratch scouting helper: python scout.py SITE PATH [PATH...] -> dumps text + links of each page."""
import asyncio, json, sys, re
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
SC = json.loads((HERE / "scouting.json").read_text())
STATE = HERE / "state"
STATE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


async def login(page, site):
    acc = next(a for a in SC["access"] if a["siteId"] == site)
    await page.goto(acc["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    for _ in range(4):
        await page.wait_for_timeout(500)
        # consent walls
        for label in ["Nur notwendige", "Alle ablehnen", "Ablehnen", "Akzeptieren", "Zustimmen", "OK"]:
            b = page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile(label, re.I))
            if await b.count():
                try:
                    await b.first.click(timeout=2000); await page.wait_for_timeout(400); break
                except Exception:
                    pass
        pw = page.locator('input[type=password]')
        if await pw.count():
            user = page.locator('input[type=text],input[type=email],input:not([type])').first
            await user.fill(acc["credentials"]["username"])
            await pw.first.fill(acc["credentials"]["password"])
            await pw.first.press("Enter")
            await page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
            return acc
    return acc


async def dump(page, maxc):
    out = []
    for i, fr in enumerate(page.frames):
        try:
            t = await fr.locator("body").inner_text(timeout=3000)
        except Exception:
            t = "?"
        out.append(f"[frame {i} {fr.url}]\n{t[:maxc]}")
        try:
            links = await fr.locator("a[href],iframe[src],form").evaluate_all(
                "els=>els.map(e=>e.tagName+' '+(e.getAttribute('href')||e.getAttribute('src')||e.getAttribute('action')||'')+' | '+(e.innerText||'').trim().slice(0,60).replace(/\\n/g,' '))")
            out.append("LINKS: " + " || ".join(links[:120]))
            inputs = await fr.locator("input,select,textarea,button").evaluate_all(
                "els=>els.map(e=>e.tagName+'['+(e.name||e.id||'')+':'+(e.type||'')+']'+(e.innerText||e.value||e.placeholder||'').trim().slice(0,40))")
            out.append("CONTROLS: " + " ; ".join(inputs[:120]))
        except Exception:
            pass
    return "\n".join(out)


async def main():
    site = sys.argv[1]
    paths = sys.argv[2:]
    maxc = 30000
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        sf = STATE / f"{site}.json"
        ctx = await b.new_context(storage_state=str(sf) if sf.exists() else None, viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        acc = next(a for a in SC["access"] if a["siteId"] == site)
        await page.goto(acc["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(600)
        if await page.locator('input[type=password]').count() or "consent" in page.url or "login" in page.url:
            await login(page, site)
        await ctx.storage_state(path=str(sf))
        for path in paths:
            if path.startswith("click:"):
                await page.get_by_text(path[6:], exact=False).first.click(); await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)
            else:
                await page.goto(acc["url"].rstrip("/") + path, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
                await page.wait_for_timeout(900)
                if await page.locator('input[type=password]').count():
                    await login(page, site); await page.goto(acc["url"].rstrip("/") + path); await page.wait_for_timeout(900)
            print(f"===== {page.url}")
            print(await dump(page, maxc))
        await ctx.storage_state(path=str(sf))
        await b.close()

asyncio.run(main())

On your own machine there is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and nothing done with those logins counts. async def page_text(self, site: str) -> str:
        parts = []
        for frame in self._page(site).frames:
            try:
                parts.append(await asyncio.wait_for(frame.evaluate(f"({READABLE_TEXT})(document.body)"), 5))
            except Exception:
                pass
        return "\n\n".join(part for part in parts if part)

    async def paginate(self, site: str, element: int, max_pages: int = 8) -> dict:
        """Follow a model-selected next-page or load-more control through one result set."""
        page = self._page(site)
        descriptor = self.controls[site][element][1] if 0 <= element < len(self.controls[site]) else None
        if descriptor is None:
            self._control(site, element)
        signature = lambda d: (d["tag"], d.get("text"), d.get("aria"), d.get("frame"))
        wanted = signature(descriptor)
        texts = [await self.page_text(site)]
        for _ in range(max(1, min(max_pages, 12))):
            await self._control(site, element).click(timeout=12000)
            await page.wait_for_timeout(600)
            await self.inspect(site, max_chars=1000)
            text = await self.page_text(site)
            if text == texts[-1]:
                break
            previous = set(texts[-1].splitlines())
            if len(previous & set(text.splitlines())) >= 0.9 * len(previous):
                texts[-1] = text  # rows were appended to the same view
            else:
                texts.append(text)
            matches = [d["id"] for _, d in self.controls[site] if signature(d) == wanted]
            if not matches:
                break
            element = matches[0]
        # Drop page chrome repeated on every page, keeping it once.
        common = set(texts[0].splitlines())
        for text in texts[1:]:
            common &= set(text.splitlines())
        combined = [texts[0]] + ["\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if line not in common)
                                 for text in texts[1:]]
        joined = "\n\n----- next page -----\n".join(combined)
        observation = await self.inspect(site, max_chars=1000)
        return {"pages": len(texts), "text": joined[:60000], "url": page.url,
                "controls": observation["controls"], "document_urls": observation["document_urls"]}

"""Model-led parallel investigation, exact bid calculation and the signed site submission.

1. A planning call splits the investigation into parallel assignments, each on one website.
2. Each assignment runs a model tool loop in its own browser tab. Workers report typed
   evidence records to a shared board that every other worker sees, so dependent lookups
   (catalog groups, material numbers, mail keys) can start as soon as the evidence exists.
3. pricing.calculate_bid applies the brief's bid rules to the records with Decimal arithmetic.
4. A submission worker enters the calculated bid in the portal and signs it with the TAN.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import time
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import models
import pricing
import run as contract
from browser_tools import BrowserTools, calculate


def tool(name, description, properties, required):
    return {"type": "function", "function": {"name": name, "description": description,
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": properties, "required": required,
                           "additionalProperties": False}}}


SITE = {"type": "string", "description": "siteId from the run access list"}
ELEMENT = {"type": "integer", "description": "control id from the latest inspection of that site"}
BROWSER_TOOLS = [
    tool("login_site", "Open the site and sign in with its run credentials.", {"site": SITE}, ["site"]),
    tool("fill_credential", "Fill a model-selected login input with this site's run credential. Use for unusual or multi-step login forms; then choose the next button yourself.",
         {"site": SITE, "element": ELEMENT, "field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["username", "password"]}},
         ["site", "element", "field"]),
    tool("navigate", "Open a model-chosen URL on this site whose path already appeared in an observation (query parameters may change; empty means site root).",
         {"site": SITE, "url": {"type": "string"}}, ["site"]),
    tool("inspect_page", "Read the current page text (including collapsed details, tooltips and canvas labels), controls, links, frames and tabs.",
         {"site": SITE, "offset": {"type": "integer"}, "max_chars": {"type": "integer"}}, ["site"]),
    tool("click", "Click a visible control chosen from the latest inspection; may navigate or submit.",
         {"site": SITE, "element": ELEMENT}, ["site", "element"]),

    tool("press", "Press a key such as Enter, Escape or Tab on the page or a control.",

    tool("paginate", "Follow a chosen 'next page' or 'load more' control through a result set (up to max_pages) and return the text of all pages at once.",
